exercise.name: Single-Arm Cable Curl
library_steps: Attach a handle to the low pulley and hold it palm up.
Keep your elbow by your side and curl the handle to your shoulder.
Lower slowly, finish your reps, then switch arms.
exercise.one_line_summary: Standing facing a low pulley, a D-handle in one hand palm up; the upper arm stays by the side while the elbow bends from ~13 deg to ~124 deg. Biceps does the work, brachioradialis helps; the other hand rests on the hip.

setup.why: Library step; S1 trained unilateral cable curls from a low pulley.

setup.target: Standing tall facing the column, feet hip-width.

setup.why: Library step: hold it palm up.

movement.measure: upper arm from the torso side line

muscles.emg: Elbow flexors grew 7-9 % after 10 weeks of unilateral cable curls (S1); biceps clearly the main flexor in curls (S2, S3).
muscles.role: Bends the elbow; what the exercise is for.

muscles.emg: Clearly active in supinated curls, near the biceps level in parts of the rep (S2).
muscles.role: Helps bend the elbow; library secondary.
muscles.surface: Thumb side of the upper forearm.

mistakes.what_it_looks_like: The upper arm swings up as the hand rises.
mistakes.why_it_matters: Library step: keep the elbow by your side.

mistakes.what_it_looks_like: The trunk leans back to heave the handle.
mistakes.why_it_matters: The arm should do the work.

sources.citation: Larsen S, Sandvik Kristiansen B, Osteras Sandberg N, et al. 2026. The effects of shoulder extension angle on elbow flexor hypertrophy in the cable curl exercise. Front Physiol 17:1750722.
sources.what_it_gave: Unilateral cable curls from a low pulley with the upper arm by the side (neutral) vs held back in shoulder extension: elbow flexors grew ~7-9 % in both; the shoulder angle made no clear difference.

sources.citation: Marcolin G, Panizzolo FA, Petrone N, et al. 2018. Differences in electromyographic activity of biceps brachii and brachioradialis while performing three variants of curl. PeerJ 6:e5165.
sources.what_it_gave: Straight bar, EZ bar and dumbbell curls at 65 % 1RM: biceps and brachioradialis both clearly active; elbow range ~117 deg.

sources.citation: Oliveira LF, Matta TT, Alves DS, Garcia MA, Vieira TM. 2009. Effect of the shoulder position on the biceps brachii EMG in different dumbbell curls. J Sports Sci Med 8(1):24-29.
sources.what_it_gave: Standing, incline (shoulder extended) and preacher curls: biceps long head at least 50 % of max RMS in all; shoulder position shifts where in the range the biceps works hardest.

clip_check.check: Start: arm nearly straight, handle in front of the thigh
Upper arm by the side in both pictures
Fist closed on the D-handle; cable from the handle to the low pulley
Free hand rests on the hip
Biceps strongest red, forearm light red, only the working arm
